findings.source_quote: Οὐ δυσωπήσεις με περὶ τῆς οὐσίας αὐτοῦ σιωπή[σαν]τα περὶ τῆς προαιρέσεως αὐτοῦ [ζη]τεῖν μόνης.
findings.english_quote: Will you not pressure me, after I have kept silent about his essence, to investigate only his purpose?
findings.issue: The negative question changes Simon’s refusal into a question that ordinarily anticipates or invites pressure. The supplied edition prints a negative future declaration, and the following explanation that God’s essence can be discussed supports resistance to restricting the inquiry. The note’s assertion that the question form follows from οὐ is insufficient: οὐ does not itself establish interrogative force.
findings.suggested_revision: Use a negative declaration, such as “You will not pressure me into keeping silent about his essence and investigating only his purpose.” Revise the accompanying note to explain the refusal and the relationship of σιωπήσαντα to ζητεῖν. Any replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ οὕτως βουλῇ τοῦ συγκρίναντος συμβέβηκεν ὡς ἠθέλησεν ἡ τῶν κακῶν προαίρεσις.
findings.english_quote: and thus, by the intention of the one who combined them, the purpose directed against evil people arose just as he wished.
findings.issue: “Directed against” supplies an oppositional relationship not expressed by προαίρεσις with this genitive. The preceding account of destroying evil people explains the contextual association, but it does not make προαίρεσις itself mean a purpose against them. The wording also conceals the source-transparent reading “choice of evil things,” which matters to the argument about the maker’s will. The alternative is disclosed in the note, but that disclosure does not support the added relationship in the main text.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare a main rendering such as “and thus, by the intention of the one who combined them, the choice of evil things arose just as he wished.” Preserve in the note the possible personal reference of τῶν κακῶν and its contextual association with the previously described destructive purpose, without presenting “against” as expressed by the genitive. This proposed wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἄλλοι δὲ εἰς χοίρους εἰσελθεῖν πρότερον παρακαλοῦντες ἠξίουν
findings.english_quote: And did not others first plead to enter pigs
findings.issue: The draft collapses the participial pleading, πρότερον παρακαλοῦντες, and the finite request, ἠξίουν, into one verb. Their general subject matter survives, but the separately expressed act of requesting and the source’s pleading/requesting sequence do not.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain both expressions, for example: “while others, first pleading to enter pigs, made their request”. Integrate this into the continuing rhetorical question and retain the following explanation about lacking authority without consent. Review the revised sentence afresh.

findings.issue: The selected print’s anomalous apostrophe after εἰσελθεῖν is reproduced in a lexical source quotation but is not identified or explained. It should not be silently treated as an OCR error, an elision requiring restored letters, or a different supplied reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a nonblocking source-feature note quoting εἰσελθεῖν’ exactly, recording the printed apostrophe and explaining that it contributes no separately recoverable lexical content to the English. Leave the selected Greek unchanged.

findings.source_quote: οὐκ αὐτὸς αἴτιός ἐστιν ὢν αὕτη τίκτει κακῶν;
findings.english_quote: is he not himself the cause, being—this matter gives birth—of evils?
findings.issue: The English mechanically displays words but supplies no intelligible construction connecting “being,” the finite clause “this matter gives birth,” and “of evils.” No defensible continuous rendering of the supplied ὢν has been established. The source note honestly acknowledges this, but disclosure cannot turn the unresolved sequence into translated meaning. This block concerns the surviving construction, not the printed lacunae: the five-dot and six-dot gaps are explicitly retained and appropriately documented.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide a defensible syntactic account of the verified supplied reading ὢν, or document and authorize an emendation in a separately identified revised source. The proposed ὧν would permit a relative construction, but it remains a conjecture rather than the selected reading and must not be adopted silently. Further confirmation of the already verified print alone would not resolve the meaning problem.
